note: Two of the nine definitions, and neither is about knowing anything -- one calls it clean and enduring, the other a fountain of life and an escape from snares. Grouped because the wisdom readings crowd these out, and the corpus gives them equal standing.
'The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life' (Prov 14:27); 'He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence' (Prov 14:26).
'The fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever' (Ps 19:9).
'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge' (Prov 1:7) -- the same formula as Prov 9:10 with knowledge in the place of wisdom.
'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom' (Prov 9:10, Ps 111:10); Prov 1:7 reads knowledge for wisdom.
'I hate arrogant pride' (Prov 8:13), and 'humility comes before honor' closing the definition at Prov 15:33. Both put it against pride rather than against ignorance.
'To fear the LORD is to hate evil' (Prov 8:13).

'the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom' (Job 28:28) against 'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom' (Prov 9:10). The same two terms and a different relation between them: one makes it wisdom, the other makes it where wisdom starts. Neither book cites the other and neither remarks on the difference.
'Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom' (Job 28:28).
'the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom' (Job 28:28).
